summary: P0 propagation-cadence test on status-context.tsx FAILED to meet Garry's 30-second requirement. Logged in as Alex (member_first), navigated to /profile (Friends section, 7 seeded friends + Roy pending), then mutated frankie's manual_status server-side WITHOUT unmounting the screen and probed the badge glyph at 30s, 45s, 65s intervals. Result: the badge only updated ~60s after the server change, NOT within 30s. Effective /api/status/for-users cadence measured 60s (calls at t+1.0s, t+60.8s, t+120.7s), not the promised 30s. Root cause is a TTL race in status-context.tsx L337-357: the sweep runs at REFRESH_TICK_MS=30_000 but only re-enqueues entries where (now - entry.ts) >= BATCH_TTL_MS (also 30_000). At the t+30s tick, cache entries are ~29s old and skip staleness, so the fetch fires only at t+60s. In-place update (no remount) works correctly at t+60s+. Heartbeat cadence (60s) and backend service.py behaviour are unchanged (regression PASS). Layout/copy visually unchanged (regression PASS).

ui_bugs.issue: Effective badge-refresh cadence is 60s (worst case), not 30s as Garry demanded. TTL race between REFRESH_TICK_MS (30_000) and BATCH_TTL_MS (30_000) means every OTHER sweep tick is a no-op — at t+30s cache entries are ~29s old and pass the freshness check, so the fetch only fires at t+60s. Measured: `/api/status/for-users` calls at t+1.0s, t+60.8s, t+120.7s (60s gap, not 30s). Frankie set to `happy` at t+9s but badge still showed 🟢 at both t+39s AND t+54s; only flipped to 😊 at t+74s after the t+60.8s batch resolved.

action_items: Fix the 30s SLA in /app/frontend/src/lib/status-context.tsx. Two viable one-line changes: (a) drop BATCH_TTL_MS to 20_000 (or less) so entries always look stale by the time the 30s tick fires; OR (b) change the sweep condition on L343 from `>= BATCH_TTL_MS` to `>= REFRESH_TICK_MS / 2` (~15s) so ticks at t+30 catch entries older than 15s; OR (c) just unconditionally clear + re-enqueue every cached uid on each sweep (Garry's original ask — 'refresh every 30 seconds'). Option (a) is simplest.
After the fix, re-verify the exact same worst-case timing (mutate status ~1s after initial batch, probe at t+30s expecting the new glyph) — this is the failing scenario.
critical_code_review_comments: status-context.tsx L337-357: comment claims the sweep guarantees ≤30s propagation but math shows worst-case ≈2× REFRESH_TICK_MS because the same constant gates BOTH the interval AND the staleness check. Any future edit that keeps these two values equal will re-introduce the bug — consider decoupling them (e.g. `SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000; BADGE_STALE_MS = 20_000`) with a comment explaining the invariant `SWEEP < STALE < 2*SWEEP`.

status-context.tsx L297-298: the debounce timer is only re-armed if `queued > 0`, but if a sweep clears stale entries AFTER pendingRef was flushed, the newly-deleted entries need a timer restart. Minor edge — sweep does call `enqueue` which handles this — but worth a code comment tying the two together.

rca_of_issue: In status-context.tsx the sweep interval and cache TTL are both 30_000ms. setInterval(tick, 30_000) fires at t+30, t+60, t+90, t+120. At each tick, only entries where (now - entry.ts) >= 30_000 are re-enqueued. But the first batch arrives at ~t+1s, so at t+30s the entries are 29s old — the >= 30_000 check fails and the sweep does nothing. Only the second tick at t+60s finds the entries stale enough (~59s old) and triggers the re-fetch. This yields an effective refresh cadence of 60s. Confirmed by two independent runs: run #1 saw for-users at t+1.0, 60.7, 120.7; run #2 saw the same pattern (t+1.0, 60.8). Fix requires either shrinking BATCH_TTL_MS below REFRESH_TICK_MS, or halving REFRESH_TICK_MS to 15_000, or removing the freshness guard inside the sweep entirely.
